method.reason: Acetone's low-lying singlet excitations are predominantly valence n→π* and π→π* transitions; B3LYP is a widely used hybrid functional for such vertical TDDFT excitations and is affordable within the frozen 12-ORCA-start/4-core budget. Full linear-response TDDFT is preferred over TDA unless cost or instability requires TDA; this choice does not assert experimental accuracy.

basis.reason: A triple-zeta polarized basis provides flexible valence and polarization description for the acetone chromophore at modest cost for a 10-atom system. It lacks diffuse augmentation, so Rydberg-like or diffuse states may be less well described; this limitation will be stated in the report. No literature citation is claimed for this model-reason selection.

proposal.reason: Select the required method and orbital basis before scientific execution. B3LYP/def2-TZVP is a practical valence-excitation model for acetone under the current resource budget; the later ORCA input will explicitly use full TDDFT rather than TDA, with NRoots chosen to retain the lowest five singlet states and the report will document model limitations.
